title: I made an AI game dev toolkit to make asset creation quicker
author: ajdare
selftext: It's been a non-stop labor of love, 7-days a week, 12 hours/day for the last 6 months but I think it's coming along nicely... and I am just so excited that it's now more possible then ever for the solo dev to actually publish... tools are here for those interested: [https://sorceress.games](https://sorceress.games)

replies.author: BenTheSodaman
replies.body:
Disclaimer, I did purchase the lifetime access during my big exploratory phase of testing tools. I'm not a paid shill or an affiliate. And inevitably, I'm going to get shit for using the tool on stream someday and someone says "look you're advertising for snake oil peddler" or some dumb shit like that. So I put the disclaimer here just in case.

————

He or someone else that knows more can correct me if I'm wrong on the questions that I can answer:

You're not tied to his platform.

Having trouble finding the section for the site's coding agent settings that let me put in my own API key before now that the site layout changed. 

For the coding agent initially, I had to bring my own API key (e.g., Claude, NVidia's offering, or other.) But I can't figure out how to do it now if it's still available without a separate purchase. (e.g., early backer for the desktop tool?)

For the other generative AI stuff like the image, video, 3D, and audio generation — you can't use your own API key from what I found. So if you already have Meshy, Super Grok, Gemini AI Pro, MageSpace on a paid account, or something that let's you generate visuals, you can just use that and upload it over if you wanted to play around it. Or if you already have an audio or voice generation service like suno dot ai (more so for music, far less so for sound effects) or Eleven Labs you can do that too. 

The cons are if you have another service you're already using that offers you more generations for what you're paying, this site is not going to beat the amount of generations you get with that if you're using the site until you go up against the wall of "you can't generate anymore" or "you've generated so much, we think you're a bot — enjoy your temporary ban."

If you're not signed up for anything yet, then getting access to the equivalent of 3\~4 separate subscriptions with credits that don't time out, and simultaneous access to models that aren't usually available under a single roof could be of interest to some. 

If you can generate any of these locally in a timely manner or on another site, you can do that too.

And if you can vibe code all the tools that his site has, it may take some tinkering, a good amount of the time (or months), and a chunk of tokens to do so. And you may run into trying to solve the same sets of issues that he's already taken a shot at and at least acknowledge they are issues versus someone else that may say "Oh it's perfect!" when there are glaring flaws with it. So a number of us may end up reinventing the wheel to make local tools or hunt down something on git to do something similar. Just up to you what route you want to take on this. e.g., pay or find someone else that did the legwork already or do the legwork on your own and make toolkit for your own needs.

Some folks seem to watch the videos and think the product is going to wipe their asses. Neither the videos or the site promises that. And their responses are very luddite-level thinking.
